top.headline: Cursor says stolen Fireworks AI key led to malicious Claude Code extension in its marketplace
top.why: A fake 'Claude Code' extension got into Cursor's marketplace. If you install coding-agent extensions, check what you have and rotate any API keys.
points: Cursor confirmed a security breach on 14 Nov (BleepingComputer, The Hacker News headlines).
Cursor attributes it to an API key exposed at Fireworks AI, used to plant a trojanised extension impersonating Claude Code.
Scope of installs and exposed data not established in the material I saw.
top.next: Cursor post-incident details and any Fireworks AI statement; no date

top.headline: GTA VI gets another day-one patch, about 1GB bigger on Xbox, days before launch
top.why: Leave room on the drive and expect a download on launch night.
points: IGN (16 Nov): a further day-one patch is coming, roughly 1GB larger on Xbox than on other platforms; full sizes not confirmed.
Launch is 19 Nov, with some regions able to play from 18 Nov because of unlock times (VICE, 15 Nov).
Unconfirmed: GAMINGbible reports boxed-copy codes were stolen; no Rockstar statement seen.
top.next: Launch 19 Nov (18 Nov in some regions); check Rockstar's channels for exact unlock time.

stories.headline: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra helped prove a lattice definition of the Standard Model
stories.why: A concrete claim of an AI model contributing to theoretical physics proof work, published alongside a new OpenAI science blog. It is a company claim until independent physicists review it.
points: OpenAI post dated 15 Nov: a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model, with GPT-6 Astra said to help turn the idea into a detailed proof.
Launched same day: a new OpenAI blog for science with findings and researcher accounts.
Not independently verified; I could not open the full post, so details are from OpenAI's feed summary.
stories.next: Independent expert reaction and any arXiv preprint; no date set

stories.headline: Pope Leo's Peru visit: 500,000 at Chiclayo Mass, abuse survivors press for more on Sodalitium
stories.why: Leo's first return to the diocese where he served as bishop mixes the pastoral (huge crowds, justice themes) with an unresolved abuse accountability question.
points: RNS (14 Nov): Vatican estimates put the Chiclayo desert Mass at about 500,000, in temperatures near 90F, with some waiting 14 hours.
Premier Christian News (15 Nov) reports Leo saying cries for justice are going 'unanswered' in remote Peru.
RNS (13 Nov): he was due to return to Zaña, where he helped found a school, to celebrate a Peruvian saint and meet marginalised groups.
RNS (13 Nov): survivors say Sodalitium's suppression stays a declaration without concrete Vatican follow-through to dismantle the group.
stories.next: Remaining Peru itinerary dates not confirmed in sources seen; watch for any Vatican statement on Sodalitium follow-through.

stories.headline: Israel opens Bar Kokhba-era hiding tunnels and a Byzantine church to the public
stories.why: Rare public access to physical evidence of the second Jewish revolt against Rome and of Byzantine Christianity in the Judean foothills.
points: Haaretz and the Jewish Chronicle (13 Nov) report Jewish revolt tunnels and a Byzantine church opened to visitors.
Jerusalem Post (14-15 Nov) names the Horvat Burgin complex and a new visitors centre at the site.
Sources were Google News listings only; I could not open the articles, so site details and dating are unverified here.
stories.next: No date given; confirm opening details with the Israel Antiquities Authority.

Company-reported results; trial design, n and follow-up not seen.
